records.title: Portfolio Archive
records.abstract: An open-source 3D archive terminal, RhineLabUI, rebuilt as a game developer portfolio: works stand on a shelf as game cases, the disc goes into a console and loads on a monitor, and an original console-style boot sequence opens the site.
findings: Built on the upstream project's 3D array, glass materials and drag interaction.
Added game case, console and monitor models generated from Blender scripts, the disc insert and loading flow, and the boot sequence.
Reworked the palette, particles, profile and project pages, and removed all third-party IP content.

Home: featured works on the shelf
The console and monitor assemble before the disc goes in

records.title: LOCKDOWN
records.abstract: A household survival game set during a pandemic lockdown. Each day you open the delivery, read messages from family and the news, keep the fridge in order, and cook for everyone at home. Cooking is a spatial puzzle: cut ingredients into shapes and fit them into the pan, tangram style.
findings: Cooking as a tangram-like puzzle: cut, rotate and fit ingredient pieces into the pan.
Fridge storage as a grid inventory where food spoils if left too long.
Daily loop of deliveries, family messages and news that shape what the household needs.

gallery.caption: Meal preparation: fitting cut ingredients into the pan

records.title: Trail Adventure
records.abstract: A first-person game about climbing and wildlife photography. An old photographer leaves you his cabin, his camera and a mountain island. Pack your bag, climb any rock face, creep up on the animals, and send your best shots to the people who live on the island.
findings: Climb anywhere steeper than 50°, on one stamina bar that hunger, cold, tiredness, injury and bag weight each eat into.
Photos are scored from one to three stars (close-ups, flight, eye contact, golden hour) and fill a field guide of 24 species.
The island, its cave and the old mine are generated in the editor, and the whole journal-style interface is drawn in code.
